lead.tldr: Bitcoin rebounds to $77k after Middle East peace deal, offsetting recent $2.26bn ETF outflows • Clarity Act pushes DASPs toward active yield‑as‑a‑service, unlocking institutional capital for compliant treasury solutions • Hyperliquid surge and AI‑linked tokens identified as catalysts for next altcoin rally. Solana positioned as long‑term infrastructure bet • Persistent higher‑for‑longer rates and oil‑driven inflation keep Bitcoin underperforming traditional assets, risk of further downside

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Bitcoin slipped amid $2.26 bn ETF outflows, a pending Clarity Act could unlock yield‑as‑a‑service, and AI‑linked altcoins such as Hyperliquid are fueling rally optimism. Meanwhile, Bitcoin’s recent bounce toward $77k suggests it may outpace stocks, bonds and gold as rates stay high.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin tanks to $74,300 as spot ETFs bleed $2.26 billion in two weeks
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin slipped to about $74,300, roughly 10% below its early‑May peak, as rising U.S. and global bond yields reduced appetite for risk‑on assets. In the same period U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange‑traded funds saw outflows exceeding $2.26 billion, the largest redemptions recorded in recent weeks. The outflows indicate that speculative capital is moving away from Bitcoin toward commodities. Analysts also note that some of the redirected funds may be positioning for a potential SpaceX initial public offering.

top_signals.title: Clarity Act could usher in a new era of crypto ‘yield-as-a-service’
top_signals.summary: The proposed Clarity Act would prohibit digital asset service providers from offering passive, hold‑to‑earn yield products. This restriction would shift the market toward active, compliance‑focused “yield‑as‑a‑service” offerings. According to STBL’s Joe Vollono, the regulatory certainty created by the Act could attract large‑scale institutional capital. He also says it could enable a new infrastructure layer for AI‑driven treasury, lending and collateral tools.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin prices news: BTC heads back to $77,000 on Middle East peace deal
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin rallied to around $77,000 after President Donald Trump announced a Middle‑East peace agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The surge came after a sharp dip earlier in the weekend, indicating renewed risk appetite among traders. At the same time, broader cryptocurrency markets displayed mixed performance, with AI‑focused tokens posting gains. Conversely, total value locked in decentralized finance protocols declined, highlighting sector‑specific pressure.

top_signals.title: Crypto trader sees Hyperliquid, AI tokens leading next altcoin rally
top_signals.summary: Michael van de Poppe, a noted crypto trader, identifies the recent surge in Hyperliquid and the broader class of AI‑linked tokens as the primary catalysts for the next altcoin rally. He also views Solana as the preferred long‑term infrastructure platform supporting these developments. Van de Poppe points to increasing institutional appetite for tokenized equities, commodities and pre‑IPO assets and maintains that AI‑related crypto projects remain undervalued, suggesting upside potential for investors.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin price analysis: BTC set to outperform after long, difficult stretch versus traditional assets
top_signals.summary: Former Credit Suisse portfolio head Mark Connors notes that Bitcoin has ended its longest historic period of underperformance relative to the S&P 500. He argues that the cryptocurrency is now positioned to outperform equities, bonds and gold as inflationary pressures and a higher‑for‑longer rate environment weigh on traditional assets. The rally, he says, is being driven by persistent oil‑related inflation that supports risk‑on sentiment for digital assets. He also points to an expanding synergy between artificial intelligence and blockchain technology as a catalyst for further price appreciation.
